comment.narrative: for the program goal of PoD to be achieved the capacity of organizations and their staffs need to be to the standard level and as the requirement of their mandates. NIMD has been identifying capacity gaps within its own staff and the staffs of partners. There is a huge capacity need from partners in organizational (such as finance) development and thematic (such as gender) areas.
At the end of 2021 NIMD will reach 100 staff members (of NIMD and boundary partners) with capacity building trainings, exposure visits and experience sharing workshops as per identified gaps.

1. 8 participants ( 5 M, 3 F) drawn from NIMD regional staff, Electoral Management bodies, Civil Society organizations, and Non-Government organizations attended a 10-day Bridge Train the Facilitator (TTF) Training from May 28– 7, 2023, at the Sapphire Addis Hotel, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, on Facilitation Skills and relevant electoral modules.
2.NIMD held a retreat for 12 staff (6 female) and NGSS staff ( from July 7-9, 2023 at Kuriftu Resort, Bishoftu. The retreat aimed to recharge and strengthen team dynamics through team-building activities and workshops. It fostered collaboration and communication, leading to increased productivity and a more cohesive work environment. The retreat included experience sharing, presentations on staff achievements, challenges and lesson learned, team-building exercises, and interactive engagements fostering camaraderie and trust among employees. It aimed to create a positive work culture that values teamwork, continuous learning, and mutual support.

The Ethiopian Political Joint Council (EPPJC) held a meeting and established three wings: Youth, Women, and Persons with Disabilities. NIMD supported the Women wing's efforts to increase women's representation in politics. Seven executive committees were selected to lead these wings, with three members being EDAC alumni. A dialogue on "Transitional Justice and Democracy for Successful National Understanding" was held and attended by a lot of participants from political parties, civil society organizations, the Ministry of Peace, and other organizations. The EPPJC has held various meetings to address various issues, including the upcoming elections in different places, the imprisonment of political party members, budget allocation by NEBE to political parties, and other political issues. The dialogue also involved NEBE and EPPJC addressing major issues and signing an MOU.

comment.narrative: the current institutional capacity of the DIs is not at the level of reaching to the citizens level to encourage citizen direct participation in the democratic space. Moreover, at the regional level the oversight and control capacity of the legislative is not comparable with the muscles of the executive body.

In the inception phase of POD there are discussions and planning started with the three DIs which will be increased to five by the end of the year. DIs will have improved relation with citizens and citizens will be encouraged to participate in the democratic space through MP citizen relation, conscious actions designed to involve citizens and their associations to participate in the democratic space

1. With the objective of improving transparency and accessibility, NIMD supported the development of a mobile application called BRIDGE (Bridging Research and Innovation for Democratic Governance and Enhanced Participation—BRIDGE for Participation) under the project called "Enhancing Participation through an E-Democracy Platform for Members of Caffee and Citizens in Ethiopia." The mobile app is in different languages (Afaan Oromo, Amharic, and English) and are ready to be used by Caffee Oromia for the purpose of sharing reports, proclamations, and minutes with the 504 caffe members, data capturing, communication, staff interaction, and connecting the caffee members with their constituents. The mobile application has a version of Websites where there is an admin page for Caffe to administer the website. The websites incorporated sections like about caffe, calendar of events, laws of the council (in languages of Afaan Oromo, Amharic, and English), and profiles of all members of Caffee as well as a section where Constituents can ask questions to the MPs
2. As part of building the full monitoring and evaluation system of the HoPR, NIMD supported the HoPR starting from the preparatory works until the automation, such as an introduction meeting for HoPR experts to discuss the data collection tools and methodology of the baseline survey, which is the prior phase of automation, the development of tools for conducting surveys, and the actual work of the survey. Apart from that, the foundation for automation, which includes the design of SPSS, data entry and analysis, and the baseline report, is done, and the system is now being automated. As part of the automation, data encoding is completed, and the results of the system, such as report generation, are already tested. Once the automation is completed and the system starts to operationalize.
